Build the training folders for BirdNET-Analyzer

Source: R/training.R
build_training_set.Rd

Splits the reviewed clips into a training and a test set and copies them into the folder layout that the training script of BirdNET-Analyzer expects: one folder per class, named after the label (species_code, so the retrained classifier keeps the labels of the current one), with the negatives of a class in a folder with the same name prefixed by -. The test clips go to a separate test folder, to be passed as --test_data.

Usage

build_training_set(
  validation,
  output_dir,
  split = c("site", "night", "site_species_night", "none"),
  test_sites = NULL,
  test_prop = 0.2,
  seed = 2026,
  max_per_site_species = NULL,
  exclude_from_test = NULL,
  negatives = TRUE,
  min_files = 100,
  copy = TRUE,
  remap_from = NULL,
  remap_to = NULL,
  strict = FALSE
)

Arguments

validation

Reviewed clips, as returned by classify_review(), post_validation() ($validation) or read_validation_tables(). It needs site, species_code, clip_file, verdict and reviewed_path (the path where the review left each clip), and night for the splits by night.

output_dir

Output folder; train/ and, if any clip is held out, test/ are created in it.

split

How to split the clips into training and test sets; see Splits.

test_sites

Sites held out for testing with split = "site". NULL puts every clip in train/.

test_prop

Proportion of the nights of each site (or site x species) drawn for the test set.

seed

Seed of the draws.

max_per_site_species

Optional maximum number of positive training clips per site x species. Larger sets are reduced by taking clips from the nights in turn, in random order, which keeps as many nights as possible. Test clips and negatives are not reduced.

exclude_from_test

Optional table with site and night (e.g. from training_nights()): nights that must not be in the test set, such as nights whose recordings trained another classifier that will be compared on it. They are left out of the draw and stay in the training set.

negatives

Include the negative clips, in -<species_code> folders.

min_files

Minimum number of positive training files per class below which a warning is raised.

copy

Copy the clips? With FALSE, only training_set.csv is written, so that the split can be built on a computer without the clips and copied later.

remap_from, remap_to

Optional prefix of reviewed_path and its replacement, for clips reviewed on another computer or drive.

strict

Raise an error if any check is above 0?

Value

A tibble with one row per clip: site, species_code, verdict, set ("train" or "test"), class_folder, clip_file, source_audio, clip_start, clip_end, from, to and night, invisibly, with the checks in the attribute "checks". With copy = TRUE, clips that could not be copied are left out.

Details

The layout follows the documentation of BirdNET-Analyzer (version 2.4.0, birdnet_analyzer.train), which also recommends at least 100 files per species; classes below min_files in the training set raise a warning. Whole-recording clips of "random_recordings" (longer than 3 s, confidence = NA) are left out: their label says only that the species was heard somewhere in the recording.

The table of clips is also written to training_set.csv in output_dir; keep it with the classifier, to leave these clips out of later validation rounds with exclude_training_clips().

Splits

Clips of the same night are correlated, so a split by clip leaks information from the training into the test set.

  • "site": the clips of test_sites form the test set, which then measures transfer to sites the classifier was not trained on.

  • "night": in each site, ceiling(n * test_prop) of its n nights are drawn for the test set, for all species together, so that no recording is training data for one species and test data for another.

  • "site_species_night": the nights are drawn within each site x species with at least two nights (the split of the 2.x scripts of the FrogNet project). The same night can then be in the training set for one species and in the test set for another, which breaks the independence of the test set; it is kept only to reproduce earlier training sets, and warns.

  • "none": every clip goes to the training set.

The draws use seed (and seed + 1 for max_per_site_species) and leave the global random number generator as it was. They follow the order of the rows of validation: the same clips in another order give another split.

Checks

At the end, three counts are reported, and kept in the attribute "checks" of the result: test nights (site x night) that also have training clips, test nights listed in exclude_from_test, and test clips that overlap a training clip of the same species in the same recording. All should be 0 with split = "night". With strict = TRUE, any count above 0 is an error.

See also

training_nights(), exclude_training_clips(), vignette("retraining").
